records.Concise description: An Ordinals goose collection derived from the CC0 generative-art lineage around Dmitri Cherniak’s 'The Goose,' with project governance and current lifecycle still insufficiently verified.
records.Deeper researched summary: Goosinals adapted a recognizable goose visual motif into an Ordinals collection and remains indexed by major Ordinals marketplaces. The underlying art/software lineage traces to Dmitri Cherniak’s CC0 work, but that does not establish Cherniak as founder or operator of Goosinals. The QA pass still did not locate an authoritative project-controlled source establishing the organizer, canonical scope, or current project operation. MSC therefore retains UNCERTAIN lifecycle status and LOW source confidence; marketplace persistence alone is not enough to call the project active.
Creators / founders: Dmitri Cherniak — source-art/software lineage only; not attributed as Goosinals founder
records.Launch / history: Ordinals-era collection from the 2023 ecosystem; current indexes show approximately 10,000 items.
records.Why it matters in the Ordinals ecosystem: Goosinals illustrates CC0 remix culture and how recognizable generative-art motifs were reinterpreted within early Ordinals collecting.
records.Verification basis: Current marketplace/indexer presence and historical ecosystem references; no authoritative project-controlled source located in the August 2026 QA pass.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not identify Dmitri Cherniak as Goosinals founder; his role is source-art/software lineage only.
Founder/organizer, exact canonical supply, and current project operation remain unresolved.
Marketplace/indexer persistence is not sufficient evidence for ACTIVE status.

records.Concise description: A 3,333-piece witch collection inspired by the Taproot Wizards and original Bitcoin Wizard cultural lineage, with lunar/dynamic visual themes.
records.Deeper researched summary: Taproot Witches uses a witch counterpart to wizard iconography and explicitly situates itself in the cultural lineage of Taproot Wizards and the older Bitcoin Wizard meme. Its official site/manifesto describes a 3,333-piece collection and emphasizes art/community over a conventional roadmap. The project retains a current first-party web presence.
Creators / founders: Project team / individual creator names not locked from the current first-party documentation
records.Launch / history: Launched in the post-Taproot-Wizards Ordinals PFP era; current site remains available in 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Ordinals ecosystem: It demonstrates how quickly Ordinals created its own derivative mythologies and visual lineages around Bitcoin-native memes.
Research notes / uncertainties: Individual team/founder attribution remains unverified from first-party sources.

records.Concise description: Metagood’s long-running on-chain art project, whose OCM Genesis collection migrated/teleburned from Ethereum to Bitcoin Ordinals and became a notable recursion and provenance case study.
records.Deeper researched summary: OnChainMonkey predates Ordinals as an Ethereum collection, but Metagood moved OCM Genesis onto Bitcoin using a teleburn process and has continued building Bitcoin-native works such as OCM Dimensions. OCM Genesis is also cited in Ordinals technical documentation as an early recursion example. MSC should keep OCM as one canonical umbrella profile and model Genesis, Dimensions, and migration mechanics as relationships rather than duplicate project pages.
records.Launch / history: OCM Genesis originally launched on Ethereum in 2021. Bitcoin inscription work began in 2023, with the Genesis teleburn migration completed/announced in late 2023; further Bitcoin-native OCM releases followed.
records.Why it matters in the Ordinals ecosystem: OCM is a major bridge between pre-Ordinals NFT history and Bitcoin-native inscription techniques, while also providing a practical early example of recursion at collection scale.
records.Verification basis: Current OCM first-party material plus official Ordinals technical documentation.
Research notes / uncertainties: Keep OCM Genesis and Dimensions as related releases under one umbrella profile unless Master Registry later requires collection-level children.
Explain teleburn carefully; do not imply Bitcoin protocol itself recognizes Ethereum provenance.

records.Concise description: A 104-piece rare-sat and recursion-oriented Ordinals art project by const_quary, organized into 8 red, 8 blue, and 88 green works.
records.Deeper researched summary: Launch-era documentation consistently describes Apostles of Greed as a 104-piece project—8 red, 8 blue, and 88 green—created by const_quary and using rare/palindrome sats with recursive submodules. Current indexers expose a much larger Apostles-branded scope in the thousands, but the QA pass found no authoritative explanation showing that those later indexed items redefine the original launch collection. MSC therefore treats the canonical original project as a completed HISTORICAL 104-piece work and preserves the larger index discrepancy as an unresolved indexing/scope note rather than allowing it to override launch-era evidence.
records.Launch / history: Launched in October 2023 as 104 works: 8 red, 8 blue, and 88 green, using rare/palindrome sats and recursive modules.
records.Why it matters in the Ordinals ecosystem: The project combines rare-sat provenance with modular/recursive art and is a useful example of how collector metadata can diverge from original project scope over time.

Corroborating sources.label: CoinGecko — Apostles of Greed current index

records.Verification basis: Consistent launch-era project documentation for the 104-piece structure and const_quary attribution, plus current indexers showing a broader unexplained Apostles-branded scope.
Research notes / uncertainties: Canonical original launch scope is 104 works; current indexer counts in the thousands appear to use a broader collection/indexing scope that remains unexplained.
Do not publish a larger 'supply' as though it supersedes the original 104-piece project without a first-party explanation.
Creator attribution should remain const_quary; a legal-name expansion is unnecessary without direct first-party confirmation.
